title: Crisp Masala Dosa with Spiced Potato and Tomato Chutney
summary: A fermented rice and urad dal batter spread thin and crisped on one side, rolled around spiced potato masala, served with a tangy tomato chutney and yoghurt.
equipment: 25-28 cm cast-iron or non-stick frying pan or flat griddle

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
waxy potatoes, boiled, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
fine sea salt or table salt
tinned whole tomatoes, crushed by hand
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Rinse the rice and cover with 1 litre cold water. Rinse the dal and fenugreek together and cover with cold water. Leave both to soak for 4-6 h.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Drain separately. Blend the rice with 240 ml cold water to a smooth paste, about 10 min in batches. Blend the dal and fenugreek with a little water until fluffy and smooth. Grinding the dal separately whips air into it, which helps the batter rise.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Whisk both pastes together in the large bowl with enough water to make a thick pancake batter, about 1.4 litres in all. Cover with the towel and leave somewhere warm for 8-12 h until bubbly and risen. Stir in the batter salt. Fermentation gives the dosa its light texture and gentle sourness.

steps.title: Make the chutney
steps.text: Heat the oil in the saucepan over medium-high heat and add the mustard seeds; when they pop, add the urad dal and chilli flakes for about 1 min until the dal is golden. Add the garlic until it just sizzles, then the tomatoes, turmeric and salt, and simmer for about 15 min until thick. Stir in the jaggery and tamarind and cook for 4-5 min more. Leave to cool.

steps.title: Make the potato filling
steps.text: Heat the ghee in the wide pan over medium heat and add the mustard and cumin seeds. When they pop, add the dried chillies and onion and cook for about 5 min until soft. Add the turmeric, asafoetida, ginger, curry leaves, garlic and green chillies for 1 min. Add the potatoes and water and cook, stirring, for about 5 min until the liquid has gone. Mash lightly, then stir in the salt and coriander.

steps.title: Cook the dosas
steps.text: Heat the griddle over medium heat and wipe it with a little oil on kitchen paper. Pour 60 ml batter into the middle and at once spread it outwards in a spiral with the back of the ladle to about 20 cm. Drizzle 1/2 tsp oil around the edge and cook on one side only for 2-3 min, until the edges dry and lift and the underside is crisp and brown.

steps.title: Fill and serve
steps.text: Spoon about 80 g filling in a line down the middle, fold the sides over to make a roll and serve at once with the chutney and yoghurt. Wipe the pan with the oiled paper and repeat with the rest of the batter.

tips: The commonest mistake is a pan that is too hot: the batter sets before it spreads. Sprinkle a few drops of water on the pan and wait until they sizzle away gently.
In a cool kitchen, ferment the batter in the oven with only the light on.
The first dosa is often a test; adjust the heat and batter thickness after it.
Leftover batter makes thicker uttapam pancakes topped with onion and chilli.
storage: Batter keeps refrigerated up to a week and filling up to 2 days. Dosas are best cooked to order; reheat filling until piping hot (74 °C). Chutney keeps refrigerated up to 2 weeks. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
